findings.claim: The `testers` array is computed unconditionally on every `asymmetricMatch` call, even when neither operand is an asymmetric matcher (the common case), adding an allocation + O(n) filter to a very hot deep-equality path.
findings.rationale: `asymmetricMatch` is invoked for every pair of values during recursive `equals`. Both `asymmetricA`/`asymmetricB` false is by far the most frequent outcome, and in that case the filter result is discarded. Moving the `filter` inside the two `if` branches (or memoizing it) would avoid the per-node cost. Fairly confident this is a real, if minor, performance regression on large object comparisons.

findings.claim: Filtering relies on `isSubsetEqualityTester(tester)` recognizing the subset-equality tester; if that check is identity-based it will silently fail for wrapped/bound/re-exported copies of the tester.
findings.rationale: The helper is not shown in this hunk, so I cannot verify it. If it is implemented as `tester === subsetEquality` (or a name check), any tester that has been bound, wrapped for arity/`this` handling, or imported from a duplicated copy of the package will not be filtered, and the fix will be a no-op in those cases while appearing to work in tests. Worth confirming how the predicate identifies the tester; also confirm it is imported/defined in this module.

findings.claim: Stripping the subset-equality tester from the testers forwarded to nested asymmetric matchers is a behavior change for existing callers and diverges from upstream Jest, which forwards `customTesters` unchanged.
findings.rationale: Composite matchers like `expect.objectContaining` / `expect.arrayContaining` re-enter `equals` with the testers they receive. Under `toMatchObject`, previously-passing assertions such as `expect(x).toMatchObject({ a: expect.arrayContaining([{ b: 1 }]) })` (where the array element has extra keys) will now fail because the inner comparison becomes strict. That may be the intended semantics, but it is a breaking change for users and a deliberate deviation from the linked Jest implementation; it deserves an explicit note/changelog entry and test coverage for the nested-matcher case.
